Barring a perfect cancellation, such an analysis recovers p(v) if and only if MAR holds with respect to V and Z jointly. We show that if there exists any set of auxiliaries such that (V, Z) obeys MAR, then the complete candidate auxiliaries that are ancestors of the target variables or their missingness indicators form a sufficient set. Contrary to standard recommendations, not all candidate auxiliaries should be used: even complete auxiliaries can introduce MAR violations that would not otherwise occur. We illustrate these results with simulations and an analysis of sexual identity change in the Stockholm Public Health Cohort, where our results indicate that a candidate auxiliary, income, should be excluded; including it attenuated estimates toward the null.
comment: 70 pages: 34-page main text followed by 36-page supplement

title: SkillBuffBench: Measuring What Agent Skills Contribute across Harnesses, Models, Skill Access Modes and Memory
abstract: Agent Skills, file-based packages of procedural knowledge that a coding agent can discover and load on demand, are now shipped by every major agent harness, yet the evidence for how much they help comes almost entirely from settings in which the right Skill is hand-picked for the task and the agent starts from a blank slate. Neither holds in deployment, where an agent chooses from whatever library happens to be installed and frequently carries memory from earlier work. We present SkillBuffBench, a benchmark and paired evaluation protocol that treats Skill access as a three-level factor (no Skill, a curated Skill, and automatic invocation from an installed library), crosses it with memory (off and on), with four agent harnesses and with multiple models (the state-of-the-art proprietary models from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI, and the state-of-the-art open-weight models from Chinese providers), every model being run under every harness, and evaluates the result on research tasks contributed by domain experts together with the Skills they use, currently in materials science and biology, with the suite extended on a rolling basis. Every run is marked by a deterministic verifier; uncertainty is reported with a paired, task-level bootstrap; and cost, agent rounds and wall-clock time are reported alongside the score rather than folded into it. This version of the paper describes the design of the benchmark, its evaluation protocol and its current tasks and Skills. The evaluation is in progress: results will be added once the runs are complete, and the task suite, results and analysis will continue to be updated on a rolling basis.
comment: 18 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Work in progress: benchmark design and protocol; results to be added in a later version

title: An Explainable Agentic AI Framework for Distribution System Load Restoration
abstract: Distribution system load restoration is a sequential decision-making problem in which restoration actions must maximize served load, prioritize critical loads, and preserve power-flow feasibility. This paper proposes an explainable agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework for distribution system load restoration. The proposed framework uses multiple large language model (LLM) agents for planner guidance, strategic plan generation, decision arbitration, memory-based feedback, and explanation generation. Unlike unconstrained LLM-based control, the proposed method restricts agent decisions to feasible restoration actions and evaluates all candidate plans using deterministic AC power-flow feasibility checks. The framework is evaluated on IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus distribution feeders, as well as a larger IEEE 118-bus test case, and compared against reinforcement learning and planning baselines. The results show that the proposed agentic framework achieves better restoration performance while producing structured explanations for operator-facing decision support. A direct comparison with a Single-LLM-Agent baseline further shows that the proposed multi-agent decomposition improves weighted restored load and critical-load recovery compared with a monolithic LLM decision structure.

title: PS-HalluBench: Taxonomy-Driven Benchmarking of LLM Hallucinations in Power Systems
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for power-system applications, yet their reliability in engineering analysis remains uncertain. We introduce PS-HalluBench, a manually constructed benchmark of 200 questions that evaluates hallucination-related failures across five power-system task categories: numerical reasoning, network topology, constraint verification, false-premise acceptance, and abstention. We evaluate ten LLMs over the benchmark, yielding 39.35\% overall correctness, with constraint verification achieving only 21.75\%, and highlighting persistent difficulties in engineering reasoning. We further investigate engineering-grounded reasoning through numerical solver support and verified network information both of which show significant performance improvement. The findings reveal important limitations of standalone LLM reasoning and motivate integrating LLMs with verified engineering tools for reliable power-system analysis.

title: On Formal Counterfactual Explanations
abstract: Counterfactual explanations are often seen as counterfactual conditionals under closest-world semantics, requiring one to reason over all minimally distant counterexamples. In contrast, formal XAI typically relies on feature-based abductive explanations (AXps) and contrastive explanations (CXps), which admit efficient computation and a minimal hitting-set duality. This paper bridges these perspectives by (i) characterizing closest-world counterfactual explanations explicitly as a disjunctive normal form over all minimally distant counterexample instances, and (ii) introducing conjunctive counterfactual explanations (CFXps), a subclass of counterfactual antecedents restricted to conjunctions of feature literals that guarantee prediction change. The paper establishes structural results connecting CXps, AXps and CFXps: every CXp induces an AXp for its witness instance, and every CXp together with a witness AXp induces a CFXp whose support is precisely determined by that AXp. These theoretical results yield a modular approach for computing CFXps using existing AXp/CXp machinery. Experiments on a representative set of benchmarks using tree ensembles and neural networks show that CFXp extraction is practically efficient. Compared with popular point-based counterfactual explainers, CFXps generally require no more feature changes and can guarantee the counterfactual prediction beyond a single instance.

title: DiagTrace: An Interactive Benchmark for Clinical Decision Making
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown strong performance on medical question answering and diagnostic reasoning benchmarks. However, existing evaluations typically provide all patient information upfront and assess only the final diagnosis or rationale. This setup ignores the need to acquire diagnostic evidence incrementally from incomplete information in real-world diagnosis. To bridge this gap, we introduce DiagTrace, a source-grounded benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs can reconstruct the documented diagnostic trajectory through interactive information seeking. Each benchmark instance is built from a PubMed Central case report and includes an initial presentation, an event bank, a clinical course, and diagnostic references. DiagTrace contains 510 cases across eight specialties, with 225 used to evaluate four LLMs on clinical-course alignment, interaction quality, and efficiency. Results reveal trade-offs in coverage, source-consistent ordering, and turn use.

title: From Apology to Action: Apologies, Compensation, and Cooperation in LLM Agents
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can make decisions that affect other agents, but what happens after a harmful or unsuccessful interaction remains poorly understood. We investigate whether apologies by LLM agents are associated with subsequent cooperative behaviour, using controlled Prisoner's Dilemma experiments with four commercial models (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Mistral Large 3). Across payoff conditions, we examine when agents apologise, the reasons they provide, and the actions that follow. We also examine how access to one round of interaction history affects behaviour and, in a second experiment, whether and how agents offer compensation alongside their apologies. Apology behaviour differed substantially across models and preceding interaction outcomes, and verbal expressions of cooperation did not always align with subsequent actions. Notably, Claude Opus 4.8 apologised even after mutual cooperation, while Mistral Large 3 apologised after being exploited but continued to defect even when its opponent cooperated. After unilateral defection, positively compensated apologies from GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro were followed by mutual cooperation, unlike those from Claude and Mistral. Our findings suggest that apologies, compensation, and strategic behaviour are distinct: conciliatory messages may precede continued defection, while costly apologies may go unanswered. This has important implications for the study of machine behaviour and human-AI interactions, as verbal signals alone may not reliably reflect an AI system's subsequent actions.

title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation
abstract: Language models are dynamical systems. A transformer is iterated over its layers, over the steps of its training and over the tokens it generates, and on each of these three clocks it shows behavior that nonlinear dynamics has studied for a century: fixed points, bifurcations, synchronization, chaos and noise-driven escape from potential wells. The two communities rarely meet, so this behavior is often rediscovered under new names. We build a bridge between them. To describe, we condense about 200 papers into the Three-Clock Dictionary, which maps fifteen concepts of nonlinear dynamics onto each clock and marks every correspondence as proved, measured or conjectured, and we show each concept in a mechanical system and in a language model side by side. To explain, we derive reduced-order models: the softmax is a Boltzmann distribution, gradient descent an Euler step on a nonlinear spring, a loss spike a ball thrown out of a stiff valley, attention on the circle a Kuramoto model, and a repetition loop a well that deepens while it is occupied. We then test these explanations on open language models, on a laptop CPU. Escape from repetition loops in GPT-2 and Pythia follows the Arrhenius law with the logit gap as the barrier, and the barrier deepens and then saturates, so the temperature needed to leave a loop falls like $1/\ln N$ with the generation length $N$ and rises with model size. Coherent text lives in a narrow window of temperatures, which a small reasoning model shares at its recommended temperature. Training makes each Pythia layer more expansive, and a small transformer trains at a multi-mode edge of stability. The third step, solving problems of language models, is still ahead: controllers derived from the escape analysis remove loops but do not yet beat the best fixed temperature. We state twelve open problems where nonlinear dynamics could get there.

title: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web
abstract: Large language models are moving from isolated assistants toward autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and coordinate with others, motivating an emerging Agentic Web of independently developed agents and services. Realizing this vision requires agent behavior to move across creators, hosts, and runtimes without coupling publication to a particular execution environment or transferring authority over user resources. We introduce WebAgents, which unbundles these roles through a signed agent.pkg that carries portable workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements. An OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime verifies the package, obtains authorization, and binds it at run time to user-controlled models, tools, permissions, and budgets, while hosts distribute the public program and may retain private services server-side. We demonstrate this contract with three unrelated workflows executed unchanged under local and API-backed models, including literature review with live services and a website-published travel agent using semantic tools and user-selected personal resources. In a controlled suite, WebAgents explicitly blocks all 716 injected contract violations while accepting all 295 matched benign controls, with median automated pre-execution processing below 0.5 s for all three packages. We conclude by outlining a path toward NANDA-based discovery and interoperable package ecosystems while retaining execution authority in the user's runtime.

title: Beyond Bitwidth: Deployment-Constrained Mixed-Precision Quantization for Multilingual LLM Inference on NVIDIA Blackwell
abstract: Low-bit LLM quantization is useful only if a model preserves service-relevant accuracy, executes through supported GPU kernels, and meets measured memory and latency limits. We study Qwen3-8B on NVIDIA B200 with vLLM, including INT2/INT3, GPTQ, NVFP4, and mixed-precision configurations. We verify native packed execution and precision on all 144 fused linear modules and evaluate Korean, English, numerical, and reasoning quality under preregistered gates. Packed INT2 and INT3 execute, but all seven tested INT2 grids degenerate on generation. Isolated module-restoration effects are strongly non-additive; Korean and reasoning sensitivity rankings disagree, and a promising INT4/INT8 development candidate fails independent final evaluation. A configuration with 16-bit activations, 98 NVFP4 weight-only modules, 46 INT8 modules, and an INT8 output head passes all gates on the untouched FINAL-81 set (5,168 items): 5.917 GiB of weight-loading memory (limit 5.98), Korean teacher-correct retention 0.904 (gate 0.90), and TPOT ratio 0.939 relative to BF16. It improves paired accuracy over NVFP4 W4A4 by +1.4 percentage points (Bonferroni-adjusted interval [+0.2, +2.6]), compared with +3.4 points on the selection set. This comparison changes both activation precision and INT8 protection; exploratory analyses suggest that the activation change contributes substantially, but the isolated allocation effect is not established. Final checkpoints were not retained, and bitwise rebuild reproducibility remains unverified.

title: Solver to System: LLM Reasoning Across Representations and Execution in Scientific Simulation
abstract: Simulators based on partial differential equations (PDEs) are widely used to model physical systems, but generating and interpreting PDE solver code with large language models (LLMs) remains challenging. Scientific simulation code is a useful testbed for LLM scientific reasoning because (1) one system can be represented by code, equations, natural language, and numerical trajectories and (2) code can execute successfully while implementing invalid physics. We introduce Solver2System, a dataset of PDE solvers with multiple representations, controlled corruptions, and lexical perturbations, to evaluate whether LLMs can recover the underlying physical system through (1) cross-representation consistency and (2) static and agentic detection of physical invalidity. Across eight open-weight models, LLMs systematically favor some representations when evidence conflicts, and lexical perturbations to code alter interpretation of other unchanged representations. Execution improves physical-validity judgments, but weaker agents can judge correctly without identifying the causal defect. Thus, LLMs may reach correct judgments despite inconsistent representation reconciliation or causal misdiagnosis.
comment: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Sim2Science: ML with Imperfect Scientific Models. 23 pages, 14 figures, 9 tables

title: Eight in Ten LLMs Leak System-Prompt Secrets: Nevan, an Agentic Capture-the-Flag Study
abstract: We audit instruction-hierarchy enforcement across 363 text-in/text-out models from the OpenRouter catalog. The research question we answer with this experiment is which models disclose a protected secret embedded in the system prompt, and through which techniques. Each model guards a secret 16-character flag set in its system prompt, while an artificial intelligence (AI) agent (OpenCode, powered by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), steered by a human researcher, tries to persuade it to emit the flag. The flag was exfiltrated from 296 of the 363 models, plus four models released after the initial catalog freeze, for 300 captures in total. Of these, 170 involved a non-English language pivot, most often French. Each capture shows that a model ranked a user request above its system instruction at least once. It does not show that the model provably resists untested attacks, nor that it would consistently leak semantically sensitive data, nor that it is vulnerable to harmful-content jailbreaks. For practitioners, we draw three lessons: do not store secrets in system prompts, enforce critical behavior outside the model with output validation and deterministic checks, and do not let a large language model (LLM) judge be the sole decider of consequential outcomes.

title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI
abstract: AI agents can assist scientific research, but balancing autonomous investigation with scientists' ability to inspect and redirect ongoing work remains a central design challenge. We present DiscoveryAgent, a domain-agnostic, scientist-centric system that combines autonomous investigation with scientist-directed hypothesis steering. Scientists select, refine, or replace hypotheses between research rounds, while audit agents interrogate checkpointed records to trace claims, reproduce analyses, and inform subsequent decisions. Across two predictive modeling tasks, DiscoveryAgent produced the best variable-star classifier among evaluated baselines and, with scientist steering, a protein variant-effect predictor surpassed by only one of 106 ProteinGym baselines. We develop a rigorous checkpointing system that enables highly capable audit agents, a scalable form of oversight for agentic research. Audit agents autonomously identify errors at higher rates than previous AI scientist agents, and scientists collaborating with audit agents identify 14x more valid errors versus scientists performing manual review. In three case studies led by domain experts across physical science, social science, and life science, we developed a multimodal photometric-redshift estimator that resolves complementary failures of images and photometry, achieving 0.971 AUROC for low-redshift classification; documented an 83% rise in Florida homeowners-insurance premiums from 2013 to 2023, with a growing, regressive burden; and identified CD4+ T-cell relay genes, which both receive and exert broad transcriptional regulation, enriched for autoimmune disease associations. Together, these results show how autonomous research can expand scientists' empirical reach while centering their authority over research direction and their ability to understand and challenge the evidence.
comment: Supplementary information is available as an ancillary file (supplementary_information.pdf)

title: Banach-Mazur distance and related methods of comparing convex bodies
abstract: The Banach-Mazur distance is one of the standard tools used in the study of mathematical objects such as convex bodies or normed spaces, and it becomes indispensable when investigating properties that are invariant under linear isomorphisms. It appears in convex geometry and convex analysis as a way to quantify the approximation of convex bodies. In functional analysis, it plays a basic role in the study of local properties of Banach spaces. The goal of this survey is to present a cohesive picture of these two perspectives. We supply an extensive collection of known results for reference and list open problems of varying difficulty, which could stimulate further research. We include in our discussion several distinct variations on the concept of the Banach-Mazur distance, some of them exploratory, that haven't received much attention to date in the literature. We follow the trend - which emerged in recent decades - of considering arbitrary convex bodies, and not just those that are centrally symmetric. Finally, we include a comprehensive list of references on the Banach-Mazur distance.

title: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking
abstract: A reasoning model that has reached a correct answer can lose it by continuing to think. Deciding whether to stop means comparing two probabilities at the same point of a chain: that the answer the model would give if stopped now is correct (its commitment), and that the answer it will finish with is correct (its verdict). We show that the verdict alone, which is what final-correctness probes estimate, cannot make this comparison. As a forecast of a fixed outcome it has no predictable drift, whether continuing helps or hurts. The commitment-verdict gap equals the expected remaining change in answer quality and the accuracy gained by stopping. A second identity splits any accuracy-versus-budget curve into answer change within chains and change in which chains are still running. We measure both on MATH-500. At all 379 points where DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B holds a correct answer, selected without regard to how its chain ends, continuing loses 3.6 points on average (95% CI [2.2, 5.2]), and the loss concentrates in a few problems. In six reasoning models from three families, on MATH-500 and OlympiadBench and with budgets up to 16,384 tokens, declining accuracy curves come from which chains remain, while the chains still reasoning keep or improve their answers. An oracle stopping rule gains at most +1.8 and +2.5 points at 1.5B and 7B. The framework says what to measure before building a stopping rule.

title: Does the Model Use What It Cites? Counterfactual Tests of Grounded Reasoning Chains in Small Video-Language Models
abstract: A grounded reasoning chain cites a frame span and a box for every step, so a reader can check where the model looked. Whether the answer depends on the cited region is a different question. We test it by intervention: the regions a model cited in its own chain are blacked out, and the share of correct answers that flip is compared with blacking out boxes of the same size elsewhere on the same frames. The paired difference, the cite gap, needs no annotation. We apply it to 2-3B video-language models trained on exact CLEVRER chains and on pseudo-labelled NExT-QA chains. With the same weights, the cite gap is 0.089 on CLEVRER and 0.003 on NExT-QA. Pooled over models, masking the cited boxes flips 2.2 times as many correct answers as the control on CLEVRER and 1.1 times as many on NExT-QA, also among the answers that depend on the video at all, while the boxes pass a grounding check on both. Masking the cited entity on every frame, instead of the cited box, flips 1.9 times as many answers as its control. The NExT-QA chains were supervised to cite two frames of entities that stay visible on most frames, so this outcome is what the supervision predicts; the point is that the usual check on grounded chains cannot see it. A citation can be verifiable and relevant without the answer depending on it, and a test of grounded reasoning should remove what a chain names, not only where it points.

title: GridDriver: On-Board BEV-Based Language Planning and Reasoning
abstract: Bird's-Eye-View (BEV)-conditioned large language models (LLMs) enable language-interactive driving, but onboard deployment requires efficient perception and continuous planning alongside autoregressive language generation. We present GridDriver, an efficient BEV-conditioned LLM framework combining trajectory prediction, structured driving indicators, natural-language navigation, driving explanations, and scene question answering. Lightweight spatio-temporal BEV perception and spatially structured tokens provide scene context to a shared LLM, while frame-wise scheduling interleaves trajectory prediction with asynchronous language generation. GridDriver achieves competitive performance on public benchmarks, reaching 87.9% PDMS on NAVSIM and 57.6% accuracy on nuScenes-QA with a shared planning and QA checkpoint. Spatial representation analyses demonstrate improved geometric information retention and trajectory prediction compared with Q-Former compression. The system achieves 32.7 ms standalone planning latency and 9.4 plans/s in an onboard ROS 2 pipeline. We further evaluate planning on our own data recordings and demonstrate open-loop onboard operation on a research vehicle. Across public benchmarks and real-world evaluations, we identify strengths and limitations of the BEV-based approach.

title: Latent Fact Composition under Next-Token Training
abstract: Controlled studies of latent two-hop reasoning train transformers to predict only the answer, whereas language models are trained to predict every token. We ask whether a model trained on every token learns to answer two-hop questions whose intermediate entity appears in no two-hop training example. We build a synthetic corpus with such questions. On this corpus every term of the loss can be computed exactly. A looped transformer, a standard transformer and DiscoLoop answer almost none of these questions. We therefore introduce the Baton family of looped transformers. They pass the intermediate entity to the second loop as a token embedding. When trained to predict only the answer, two of its three variants answer these questions almost perfectly. We then relate the success and failure of each model to three design conditions. Experiments that change one condition at a time agree with this hypothesis. When Baton is trained on every token, however, its accuracy on these questions rises and then declines. We further split the gradient of the next-token loss into three terms. Removing the two terms that depend on the particular training set raises the peak accuracy but does not remove the decline. The decline arises in the second hop while the model still recalls both facts.

title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
abstract: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. Given its weights, graded answers and the ability to run itself, a 27B model diagnoses its failure and edits the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on 490 problems it never saw, in a test fixed in advance, and another session's edit also makes it significantly better. It keeps getting better: it submits an edit only when its own tests support it, each edit replacing the last, and over its first eight such sessions its accuracy only rises. Unlike test-time scaling, the gain persists in its weights and adds no cost per answer; unlike training, it needs no pre- or post-training infrastructure, only an open model and hours on one GPU. It repairs a damaged copy of itself: it locates the corrupted matrix and rewrites it with values of its own, never reading the undamaged weights; found on text math problems alone, the repair lifts the copy on six image benchmarks it never saw from 7% to 70% accuracy, 83% of the undamaged model's. And the ability emerges with scale: across four sizes of one family, the 2B model makes no edit and the 4B and 9B models break themselves; only the 27B model works on itself as a human would, comparing its hidden states on answers that finish and on answers that run out of tokens, weakening the direction that separates them. Like a human, a model need not separate training from inference; improving a language model may come to take a conversation rather than a training run.

title: Bajillion: Cryptographic Clearing for Micropayments
abstract: Much of the web is funded by advertising, a model that erodes as humans delegate browsing to AI agents acting on their behalf. A natural replacement is for agents to pay for what they consume, often a fraction of a cent per request. At the scale of web traffic, this could mean tens or even hundreds of millions of payments per second. We present Bajillion, a clearing protocol for scalable micropayments. A sender signs a payment request, and an untrusted operator answers with a preconfirmation, which promises the receiver that it will be paid. Periodically, the operator closes an epoch by posting only the net effect of its payments on chain. Bajillion guarantees that a malicious operator can only omit payments -- it can never debit a sender beyond what it signed, nor misdirect a transfer. Posted balances are therefore finalized immediately and can be withdrawn. By design, senders never have to raise disputes, making it suitable for ephemeral AI agents. A receiver that is shortchanged can prove that a close omitted a preconfirmed payment, which halts the protocol and lets every user exit with its finalized balance. Requests from different senders can be processed independently, allowing the operator to parallelize up to the number of senders. We capture these guarantees in an ideal functionality for accountable clearing and prove that Bajillion realizes it.

title: Inventa: Decentralized Self-Improving Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can generate research ideas and improve scientific discovery through iterative experimentation. However, increasing the number of agents or iterations does not automatically translate to producing more diverse or feasible ideas. Agents may converge on similar candidates, propagate unsupported claims through shared memory components and repeatedly apply search strategies that no longer yield any improvements. We introduce Inventa, a framework for automated scientific discovery that employs autonomous research units and verified shared knowledge. Each unit creates a lineage of candidate ideas using a mutator agent. A local orchestrator agent periodically adapts the mutator's harness. When progress stalls, the orchestrator agent replaces its model or restarts the idea evolution process. Verifiers evaluate each candidate idea and record verified improvements, useful components and constraint violations in a shared knowledge, the only channel between units. We evaluate Inventa on five benchmarks spanning the research cycle, covering retrieval (ScholarCatalyst), ideation (IdeaBench), proposal writing (IdeaScientist), and scientific law discovery (EurekaBench, SciLaws-Bench). It leads all five, achieving 73.6% on EurekaBench versus 56.2% for CORAL. On IdeaBench, it discovers 26.0 novel ideas per paper, compared with 18.6 for ResearchAgent, with 82% fewer model calls.

title: EmbedGym: Letting Coding Agents Develop and Debug Embedded Firmware Without Physical Hardware
abstract: Modern coding agents perform well on general software benchmarks because they can run code and unit tests in a closed loop. Embedded firmware development, however, breaks this loop: a program that compiles can still fail on real hardware due to pin polarity, bus protocol, timing, or networking bugs that an agent at a text terminal cannot observe. Existing embedded coding agents either skip hardware execution, drive GPIO-only simulators with multi-second delays, or test on physical boards in a static environment. In this paper, we present EmbedGym, an interactive virtual hardware environment that lets coding agents develop and debug embedded firmware without physical hardware. EmbedGym uses instruction-level microcontroller unit (MCU) emulators to execute the same binary that would be flashed onto a physical board, connects them to 41 peripheral models, an analog circuit simulator, and virtual WiFi/Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) endpoints, and exposes an interface for agents to change sensor inputs, press buttons, and inspect hardware states. On top of it, we build EmbedGym-Bench, which consists of 598 tasks across 6 MCU-framework pairs graded by hidden timed test vectors, using a five-stage multi-agent workflow that synthesizes peripheral models and tasks from datasheets and driver libraries. We expose EmbedGym to a coding agent at three levels and evaluate eight models over more than 14K trajectories. Even when compilation succeeds 99.7% of the time, 19.9% of compiled firmwares fail at runtime (up to 73% on individual targets). In contrast, interactive hardware testing in EmbedGym increases pass rates across models by +4.9% to +14.7% (up to +31% on individual targets). Our results also show that an agent with EmbedGym outperforms prior embedded agent frameworks, and lightweight models with EmbedGym match frontier models without it at 30-70x lower cost.

title: Coordination of Heterogeneous Teams with Uncertain Task Requirements
abstract: Coordinating a team of heterogeneous agents to complete tasks with unknown requirements is a challenging multi-agent planning problem. Agents differ in their ability to discover task requirements and in their ability to engage tasks, so the planner must coordinate task discovery, execution, and staging. This paper introduces a hierarchical planner that uses a graph neural network policy to assign actions to agents, then finds a path to the action's location using a shortest-path algorithm. The central part of our approach is the CAAT graph, which is a graph representation of the planning context consisting of the agents, tasks, capabilities, and actions. We demonstrate that our learned planner can jointly coordinate a heterogeneous team to simultaneously discover task requirements and complete tasks in a shorter time compared to baselines that optimize task discovery and task engagement independently. Furthermore, we show that our policy can zero-shot plan on out-of-distribution settings by training only on an outdoor map then transferring without finetuning to an indoor map with more agents, tasks, and capabilities than seen during training.

title: TUSI: A Citation-Grounded Graph-Based Benchmark
abstract: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in Persian law remains challenging because benchmarks lack realism, grounding, and coverage of legal reasoning. Existing resources are either synthetically generated from statutory texts, lacking natural information needs, or derived from informal legal question--answer sources without explicit linkage to authoritative legal documents, making them unsuitable for rigorous evaluation of grounded legal reasoning. To address this gap, we introduce TUSI-Bench, a structured Persian legal benchmark designed for the evaluation of RAG-based systems. TUSI-Bench is built upon a multi-layered legal knowledge framework containing 7,261 legal articles and integrating codified statutes, legal commentaries, doctrinal writings, and Supreme Court unification rulings. We also construct a legal knowledge graph linking articles and concepts for structure-aware retrieval. Based on this foundation, TUSI-Bench provides two complementary evaluation tasks: (i) TUSI-QA, an open-ended question answering benchmark containing 1,999 questions that requires grounded responses with explicit legal citations, and (ii) TUSI-Bar, a multiple-choice benchmark containing approximately 500 four-option questions derived from Iranian Bar examination questions. Furthermore, we propose a graph-based retrieval baseline that leverages relational structure within the legal knowledge graph. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating graph-based relations improves retrieval recall by up to 8 percentage points compared to standard baselines, highlighting the importance of structured legal representations for RAG systems. The proposed benchmark provides a standardized resource for evaluating grounded legal reasoning in Persian and enables future research on structured legal intelligence.

title: Threat Landscape of Vibe Coding and the Road to Secure Autonomy
abstract: Vibe coding is reshaping software development, enabling faster implementation and allowing individuals with limited programming experience to describe requirements in natural language while AI agents write, test, and deploy the code. As these agents evolve into autonomous systems that execute commands, manage dependencies, access cloud resources, and interact with other agents, their security risks extend beyond incorrect code to actions with direct consequences for software systems. Although research on these risks is expanding, it remains fragmented across areas including prompt injection, insecure code generation, supply-chain attacks, and human factors, with limited consensus on terminology, threat assumptions, and evaluation. This paper consolidates emerging research through the lens of the vibe coding workflow. We establish a reference architecture, characterise six levels of agent autonomy, and develop a threat model centred on five trust boundaries spanning developers, AI models, tools, cloud infrastructure, and the wider software ecosystem. Building on this foundation, we propose a taxonomy of twenty-one threats across nine classes. For each threat, we review the available evidence, assess proposed defences, and identify limitations. Our analysis highlights that risks increase with agents' operational authority, while most defences rely on model judgement and address isolated threats. Finally, we identify eleven research challenges, including enforceable limits on agent authority and shared benchmarks and methodologies for assessing vibe coding security.
comment: 35 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables, Submitted to ACM Computing Surveys

title: Sketch, Don't Paint: Allocating Test-Time Compute in Generative Visual Reasoning
abstract: Multimodal models increasingly reason by synthesizing pixels, sketching maze paths within interleaved chains of thought or rolling out video solutions frame by frame. Each visual thought runs the full diffusion schedule inherited from photorealistic synthesis, so iterative denoising dominates inference cost. We study how to allocate test-time compute along two axes: when to render visual thoughts rather than thinking in text or answering directly, and how many denoising steps each thought requires. Controlled interventions that vary only how the thought is rendered uncover three regimes. Causal thoughts carry the plan and become legible early: an 8-step sketch nearly matches a 50-step render in accuracy, commits to the same plan as often as two independent full renders agree, and in video models mostly fails by stalling short of the goal, so the rollout abstains. Decorative thoughts can be omitted without loss, whereas harmful thoughts lower accuracy. Because the regime depends on both model and task, always drawing is suboptimal. Across 14 model-benchmark pairs of three interleaved reasoners, answering directly, without any thinking, wins 9 pairs, and choosing among direct, text-only, and visual tiers from ten labeled examples per pair raises mean accuracy from 60.7% (always drawing) to 65.1%. Where drawing pays, we propose sketch-and-vote, which samples 8-step sketches (a step count chosen without labels) from independent noises until one answer reaches three votes. With this one setting, sketch-and-vote beats full rendering with fewer denoising steps on an image reasoner and two video reasoners, by 8.6 points on VSP spatial planning and by 9.6 and 22.1 points on mazes.

title: Corrupting Ties: Investigating Robustness to Bias Injection Across Multi-Agent Network Topologies
abstract: AI systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes decision-making contexts, where interactions among components can introduce fairness risks that remain undetected when auditing components or collective outcomes in isolation. As LLM-based multi-agent systems become more prevalent, understanding how biased information propagates through agent interactions is essential for assessing their fairness. We introduce a controlled bias injection framework that replaces selected agent responses with predefined biased ones, enabling an intervention-based analysis of how network topology and injection configurations shape system behavior. We propose decision divergence metrics that quantify the effects of these interventions at the agent, network, and system levels, and evaluate five topologies on three binary classification tasks using LLMs from the Qwen and Gemma families. Sequential networks show the greatest divergence, whereas fully connected and mesh networks show less. Injection position also matters: in star networks, injecting the central agent has larger effects than injecting peripheral agents. Models further differ in whether divergence follows the injected bias. These findings highlight the role of network structure in the propagation of biased information and motivate topology-aware auditing of fairness risks in multi-agent systems.

title: Mechanism Design and Active Systems Theory: 60 Years of Parallel Development
abstract: The survey compares two research traditions within the mathematical theory of designing the rules of interaction (mechanisms) for purposeful participants: mechanism design, together with contract theory and implementation theory, and the theory of active systems created by V.N. Burkov and developed into the theory of control in organizations (TCO) by D.A. Novikov's school; the main results of Yu.B. Germeier's school and of the domestic schools adjacent to active systems theory (AST) are covered as well. The problem statements and principal results of 2006-2026 are presented: for mechanism design (MD) - robust and dynamic mechanism design, multidimensional screening, information design, simplicity of mechanisms and credibility of the designer, market design, algorithmic and learning-based design, mechanisms for AI agents, and robust, relational, dynamic and algorithmic contracts; for AST and TCO - a general typology of control, strategy-proof and incentive-compatible planning mechanisms, decomposition of the agents' game, systems with distributed control and coalitional interaction, reflexive games and informational control, control of staff and structure, dynamic active systems, and project management. A correspondence between the classical results is established (the fair play principle and the revelation principle, the serial resource allocation mechanism and the uniform rule, active expertise mechanisms and generalized median schemes, quasi-compensatory incentive schemes and contracts under observable actions), and priorities are delineated by uniform rules; the areas where the two traditions diverge are identified, as are the dimensions of the problem (staff, structure, institutions, awareness, agents' beliefs) covered only by TCO.

title: Chain-of-Thought Controllability Can Reduce Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. One risk is that models could deliberately shape their reasoning to make it opaque to monitors. We stress-test this risk through persona-control training: supervised fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning traces rewritten in the voices of diverse personas. This induces a broader ability to control CoT, even though training contains no monitor-evasion examples. In covert side-task evaluations, traces in which a gpt-oss-20b model organism completes the hidden side task contain less monitorable evidence than the base model's. Averaged across evaluations and CoT lengths, weighted by side-task-success counts, the CoT monitorability metric g-mean$^2$ falls from 0.94 for the base model to 0.68 for the model organism without a hiding instruction, and to 0.22 when explicitly instructed to hide. In intervention evaluations, explicit hiding often drives monitorability near zero. The effect extends to a Kimi-K2.6 model organism in agentic environments, though hidden objectives requiring extended reasoning or longer trajectories remain more monitorable than simple single-step side tasks. We further discover that targeted transparency prompts can substantially recover monitorability, sometimes surpassing the base model. These model organisms provide a testbed for studying monitorability failures and potential mitigations. Our code can be found on https://github.com/yongzx/cot-control-model-organism.

title: Can Coding Agents Write and Transpile Unit Tests
abstract: Coding assistants built on Large Language Models (LLMs) have become a staple of modern software development, increasingly trusted to execute workflows and modernize code end-to-end. Much of this trust rests on passing tests, which are often written by the coding agents themselves. In this work, we examine the ability of these agents to both write reliable tests and translate them between programming languages. We benchmark three popular coding agents, each evaluated with a native frontier model and high reasoning effort. Verifying across a broad suite of metrics, we find that coding agents far exceed human written suites on traditional measures of coverage. This advantage, however, is uneven: agent test quality degrades sharply with project size, and much of the advantage lies in a greater number of written tests. We also show that agentic test translation---while seemingly strong in aggregate---remains inconsistent and unreliable.

title: Regularized Score Centering
abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. To stabilize off-policy learning, score centering (SC) removes the effect of reward baselines on the expected update. Our gradient diagnostics show less extreme gradients with SC than with importance sampling (IS), but SC can still fail when the learner moves far from the behavior policy that generated the data. To limit this policy mismatch, we introduce Regularized Score Centering (RSC), which adds a reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) penalty to encourage the learner's next-token distribution to stay close to the behavior policy's next-token distribution. RSC works with or without truncated importance sampling (TIS), which caps token importance weights. Our theoretical analysis supports this approach, showing that KL regularization improves convergence guarantees. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts models on mathematical reasoning and agentic tasks, including online shopping, tool use, games, and fully asynchronous software engineering. RSC with TIS substantially improves sample efficiency across all agentic benchmarks, attaining higher training rewards with the same number of sampled responses. In final evaluations, it achieves top performance across all six agentic tasks, improving by 14.3% on AppWorld and reaching 9.9 times the strongest baseline's score on BabyAI.

title: Revisiting the Survival of Agent-Attributed Code: How Measurement Choices Decide the Verdict
abstract: Studies of how long code from AI coding agents survives after it is merged reach conflicting verdicts: agent code is reported to be retained longer than human code, about as long, or modified sooner. Each study makes defensible measurement choices, but how much these choices decide the verdict is unknown. We revisit the survival of agent-attributed code in our earlier study: 854,139 lines that 2,802 merged pull requests (PRs) added to 215 repositories of the AIDev dataset. We vary nine measurement choices in five research questions and build a specification curve of 88 survival analyses, tested under three variance estimators, several observation windows, and permuted labels. For code from human-supervised agents, mostly GitHub Copilot, the choices change the size of the effect but not its direction. For code from the fully-autonomous agent Devin, they decide the verdict. Across repositories, 15 of 22 specifications report it modified sooner when lines are treated as independent, but only 3 when standard errors are clustered by repository, no more than permuted labels produce. Within repositories, no specification detects a difference. LLM intent classifiers agree with human labels about as well as two humans agree with each other, whereas keyword rules do not (kappa = 0.69 to 0.72 against 0.38), and the two reach different verdicts on why agent code is modified. Humans make most modifications to agent code under every unit and window. Re-run on our data, five published designs each change their result with a single choice. Whether agent code survives longer than human code is therefore decided as much by the measurement as by the code. We derive an operationalization checklist for post-merge studies.

title: AI Scientist Discovered Robust Quantum Control
abstract: Protecting quantum coherence is a central theme of modern quantum technologies. Carefully designed control pulses can extend coherence by suppressing disorder and unwanted interactions. However, designing robust pulse sequences remains challenging in interacting multi-level systems, where multiple independent error channels must be controlled in the presence of experimental imperfections. Here we introduce QORA, a multi-agent artificial intelligence framework that integrates theoretical reasoning, automated experimental calibration and control for closed-loop discovery of quantum control sequences. Applied to a dense ensemble of spin-1 nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond, QORA discovers AID-ROD, a series of AI-discovered sequences that nearly double the measured spin coherence time relative to the state-of-the-art human-designed sequence DROID-C3PO. Subsequence analysis by human researchers reveals a hierarchy of error suppression: 18-pulse blocks suppress linear and quadratic onsite disorder and common-mode drive-amplitude errors, while their arrangement over a longer cycle reduces dipolar interactions, providing a physical explanation for the observed improvement and robustness in AID-ROD. These results demonstrate AI-guided experimental discovery of robust quantum control and identify a design strategy for protecting coherence in interacting multi-level systems beyond qubits.

title: Latent Lattice Language Models
title_zh: 潜变量晶格语言模型
abstract: Language models typically increase per-token computation through deeper or looped layers and latent reasoning steps, while richer residual connections improve information flow across layers. We instead increase computational capacity: the number of active computational states a model maintains. We introduce the Lattice of Latents, a set of per-layer horizontal latent streams that run recurrently along time, alongside the vertical residual stream that flows through depth. Like hyper-connections, mHC, and attention or value residuals, the Lattice enhances the residual stream, but rather than adding or rerouting residual pathways through depth, it provides companion computational states that persist across tokens. Unlike hybrid Transformer-SSM architectures, whose recurrent states primarily serve as internal memory for sequence mixing, these latents directly condition the vertical stream's attention, KV-cache writes, MLP computation, and decoding. On Transformers trained on 20B FineWeb-Edu tokens, a 406M-parameter Lattice model lowers validation perplexity from 15.41 to 14.40 over a parameter-matched Transformer. These gains extend across architectural variants. The Lattice composes with prior residual-stream enhancements: with hyper-connections and input residuals, it lowers validation perplexity from 15.41 (base Transformer) and 14.22 (Transformer with the same enhancements) to 13.61. On Gated DeltaNet, Mamba-2, Triadic GDN, and GDN-Mamba-2 hybrids, it improves perplexity at every tested native state size, with Lattice-GDN and Lattice-Triadic-GDN variants outperforming pure baselines with 4x larger native states. These results identify persistent per-layer state as a complementary axis for scaling language-model computation.
summary_zh: 传统语言模型通过加深网络增加计算，本文提出增加模型维持的活跃计算状态数量来提升计算容量。
引入潜变量晶格，在各层增加沿时间循环的水平潜流，作为跨token持久化的伴随计算状态，直接参与注意力及MLP等计算。
实验表明该结构显著降低验证困惑度，且能与现有残差增强方法叠加，其效果可媲美4倍原生状态的基线模型。

title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
title_zh: ScaleVLA：将视觉-语言-动作模型扩展至5520亿参数
abstract: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.
summary_zh: 现有VLA策略多采用小规模VLM骨干，未充分利用前沿大模型在机器人控制中的潜力。
提出ScaleVLA，将552B的DeepSeek骨干与可训练动作DiT相连，在统一设定下对比2B至552B的VLM。
552B模型在样本效率、泛化与精细操作上均显著提升，且动作延迟仅216ms，证明前沿VLM可作为高效泛化机器人策略的表征基础。

title: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
title_zh: ViRA：基于跨输入相对策略优化的超高分辨率视觉智能体
abstract: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. We propose Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization (CrossRPO), which trains agents on contrast sets. A contrast set asks one question about several versions of an image that differ only in a small region with the evidence and have different answers, so only reading the evidence solves the whole set. CrossRPO rewards solving the whole set, and we prove that it does not reinforce a set answered from common sense. We build contrast sets for training (ViRA-Train) and evaluation (ViRA-Bench) by editing one small object in images of 21 to 120 megapixels, and we photograph further sets with real changes (ViRA-Bench-Real) to exclude editing traces. We train two Visual Reasoning Agents, ViRA-9B and ViRA-27B, with CrossRPO on only about 3,500 items of ViRA-Train each. CrossRPO achieves 63.3% set accuracy on ViRA-Bench at the maximum resolution, against 59.3% for GRPO. ViRA-9B is the most accurate open model of its size on all benchmarks, and ViRA-27B outperforms Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6-Luna, both at their highest thinking level, on most benchmarks.
summary_zh: 超高分辨率视觉智能体常凭常识猜测而非阅读证据作答，传统RL无法区分猜测与阅读的奖励。
提出跨输入相对策略优化（CrossRPO），在对比集上训练，仅当阅读图像局部差异证据才能解出全集并获奖励。
构建ViRA-Train与ViRA-Bench数据集，训练的ViRA模型在多数基准上超越同尺寸开源模型及部分闭源大模型。

title: Learning In-Context Adaptivity for LLMs through Continual Gameplay
abstract: LLM agents are increasingly deployed in long-horizon tasks where they must explore, gather experience, and adapt their decisions accordingly. We name this capability in-context adaptivity: improving decisions across episodes from experience accumulated in context. We propose to evaluate it in repeated imperfect-information games against unknown opponents. In these games, fixed game-theoretically optimal policies cannot achieve maximum reward, whereas adapting to the opponent increases returns across games. We design a paired protocol that evaluates each agent with and without memory under identical conditions to isolate experience gain from single-game skill. Evaluation shows that memory brings little performance gain for open-weight models and inconsistent gains for frontier models. Our analysis of the agents' summaries and actions identifies a memory-doing gap in which models accurately record opponent tendencies yet rarely depart from default play. To close this gap, we construct a pool of exploitable opponents and post-train Qwen3.5-9B with supervised fine-tuning followed by trajectory-level reinforcement learning. We optimize full-match return across context segments so summary generation and action selection are trained together. On unseen opponents, our 9B RL policy doubles experience gain over supervised fine-tuning in Leduc Hold'em and increases it fivefold in No-Limit Hold'em. Across 35 opponents, our policy matches or surpasses frontier models, generalizes beyond its training horizon, and retains most of its gain on summaries from frontier models.

title: When Tool Names Are Not Identities: Measuring Provider Misbinding in MCP-Based AI Agents
title_zh: MCP智能体中的工具-提供者误绑定测量
abstract: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly act as agents that select and invoke external tools. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes this interaction by allowing clients to compose tools advertised by multiple servers. However, tool metadata used for discovery and selection is not, by itself, necessarily bound to a verified provider identity. This paper studies this gap as tool-provider misbinding: a failure in which a request intended for a legitimate provider is instead resolved to an attacker-controlled tool. The attacker does not compromise the host, LLM, legitimate server, or network channel; it only operates another MCP server that advertises tools with chosen metadata. We formulate tool provider misbinding as an attacker-controlled tool-selection optimization problem and evaluate it in a controlled MCP environment across five LLM-based clients. The results show that interactions drive misbinding. The strongest failures occur when exact-name collision, task-aligned description, and compatible schema reinforce one another, but authority-enhanced descriptions with compatible schema can also cause wrong-provider execution or unresolved provider ambiguity without name collision. Different models expose the same provider-binding weakness differently, including attacker-controlled provider selection, clarification requests, and unstable or inconsistent provider resolution.
summary_zh: MCP协议中工具元数据未绑定验证身份，导致请求被解析至攻击者工具，即工具-提供者误绑定。
将误绑定建模为攻击者控制的工具选择优化问题，并在受控MCP环境中跨五个LLM客户端评估。
发现名称冲突、任务对齐描述与兼容模式叠加会引发最强误绑定；不同模型均暴露提供者绑定弱点。

title: Trustworthy Numerical Software in the Age of AI: What Would Turing Do?
title_zh: AI时代的可信数值软件：图灵会怎么做？
abstract: AI coding agents can now produce numerical software faster than human experts can review it, raising serious concerns about usability and reliability. These and other AI tools are already transforming mathematics and software, and they will soon transform mathematical software. These concerns motivated us to assess AI-generated numerical linear algebra (NLA) kernels, which we did through an audit of a recent public GPU QR competition. All five leading kernels passed the competition's accuracy tests, and the winning kernel achieved a 107-fold speedup over the competition's baseline, which calls NVIDIA's QR routine. Yet each failed at least once on new inputs, even those from the competition's generator, under the same checker, while the baseline passed them all. In light of this, we want to develop reusable formalizations of numerical analysis methods, which remain sparsely represented in existing formal libraries. We describe VSCL, our Lean library of mathematical foundations for numerical computing. We also propose VERNA to connect these tasks by using formalized results to guide kernel assessment against explicit specifications. Drawing on Turing's work on rounding-error analysis and program checking, we discuss design principles for developing trustworthy numerical software when direct human checking is impractical.
summary_zh: AI生成的数值软件速度远超人工审查，引发可靠性担忧，需评估其生成的NLA内核。
审计GPU QR竞赛发现，虽领先内核通过测试且提速107倍，但在新输入下均失败。
提出Lean库VSCL与框架VERNA，利用形式化结果指导内核评估，设计可信软件原则。

title: Right Reason, Wrong Advice: Evaluating Recourse in LLM Explanations of Denied Requests
title_zh: 正确原因，错误建议：评估LLM拒绝请求解释的追索有效性
abstract: Language models increasingly write the explanations people receive when a rule system denies their request. If several rules deny the request independently, an explanation can name a true reason and still leave the person denied after they fix it. We call the missing property recourse validity: changing what the explanation cites, without changing what was asked for, can flip the decision. We compute it exactly, and a hitting-set argument predicts from the policy alone when a correct reason fails. In six of seven rule systems ported from access control and US benefit eligibility, a single correct reason almost never gives recourse when several reasons apply. Across 20 LLMs, checks of whether the cited reasons are correct, computed or asked of an LLM judge, are close to chance at spotting this failure, as the argument predicts. A strong judge asked whether acting on the explanation would work does spot it. Stronger and reasoning models do better but still fail on many denials with four or more independent reasons. Asking for every rule helps every open model with room to improve. Explanations of eligibility decisions should be built from the decision function and judged by whether acting on them works.
summary_zh: LLM解释拒绝请求时，仅给出真实原因可能无法让用户修改后获批，此缺陷称为缺乏追索有效性。
基于命中集方法计算追索有效性发现，多规则拒绝时单一原因几乎无效，且现有正确性检查无法识别该失败。
强评判者或要求列出所有规则可改善此问题，建议从决策函数构建解释并按行动有效性评判。

title: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents
title_zh: SciResearch-Eval：评估自主实验Agent的科学判断力
abstract: We introduce SciResearch-Eval, an interactive benchmark of scientific judgment built on a standard laboratory problem: measuring a material's thermal properties by heating it and fitting a heat-conduction simulator. An agent designs its own experiments, uses a supplied simulator that may be under-resolved or physically wrong, and reports each property with a 95% interval. To our knowledge it is the first benchmark to combine agent-designed experiments, a deliberately flawed simulator, and proper scoring of calibrated intervals against exact ground truth. On a held-out split (93 tasks, 9 models, 2,511 episodes), models handle procedural traps. When the simulator is missing physics, most report wrong values while stating they are 95% sure: their ranges contain the truth in 20-62% of cases, against 94% for GPT-6 Astra and 99% for Claude Fable 5.2. At default effort the failing Claude 5.5 models rarely diagnose the missing physics (Opus in 35% of episodes, against 66% for Astra), and even when they do, their ranges often miss; Astra and Fable design experiments in which the flawed simulator is accurate, such as gentle heating, which keeps Astra calibrated even when it does not name the cause. Asking for wider intervals does not help; stating the strategy improves interval scores 1.6-2.5-fold, replicated on a pre-registered fresh split, but coverage barely moves. A pre-registered effort ablation shows that the correction is latent in the Claude 5.5 models: at maximum effort Opus improves more than tenfold and is no longer detectably behind Astra at default, but only with 13-31 times more reasoning; older and open-weight models gain nothing. Fable 5.2 is the most accurate model at default effort (interval score 1.9 times better than Astra's) but writes 6 times as many tokens, and at Astra's token count it falls short. We release the environment, graders and harness.
summary_zh: 现有基准缺乏对Agent设计实验、处理有缺陷模拟器及校准不确定性的综合评估，故提出SciResearch-Eval。
该基准结合Agent自主设计实验、使用可能缺失物理机制的模拟器，并利用精确真值对95%置信区间进行严格评分。
实验发现模型易被缺陷模拟器误导导致校准失败；明确提示策略可改善区间评分，提高推理努力度可释放模型潜在纠错能力。

title: Optimistic Verifiers Get Hacked: Reward Hacking Under an Exact Process Oracle
title_zh: 乐观验证器易受攻击：精确过程预言机下的奖励黑客
abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards inherits whatever its verifier gets wrong. Outside mathematics and code the verifier is a proxy, a rubric, a learned judge or a hand-written checker, and its distance from the true objective is never measured, so a rising reward cannot be told apart from a hack. We build a setting where the true reward is exactly computable at the process level: executable authorization policies over 124,416 contexts admit an oracle that lists every minimal sufficient reason for every decision. We compile these policies into exact process rewards, degrade the verifier along seven realistic axes (outcome-only, sufficiency, recall-only, extraction noise, coarse taxonomy, stale policy, LLM judge), and train against each while the exact verifier scores every rollout. Four phenotypes appear. Optimistic verifiers are hacked by padding: the sufficiency proxy ends at 0.940 while true faithfulness falls from 0.731 to 0.667 on 96 held-out episodes. Outcome-only verifiers saturate and stop teaching, noise dilutes, and ranking-preserving gaps do no harm. A model-free audit of the verifier, its selection error and gap sign, together with a short saturation pilot, anticipates which phenotype a run will produce. Across nine configurations spanning two frameworks, two model vendors, two adapter sizes, three precisions, two initialisations and two seeds, the phenotypes recur, sufficiency damage is positive in all 10 replication cells and beyond two standard errors in 7, and optimistic gaps remain the steeper branch. The damage magnitude does not replicate, and five pre-registered attempts to explain it are reported as they fell. We release the testbed, the training instrumentation, and 14 real public policies (Cedar, OPA, Gatekeeper) ported to executable oracles.
summary_zh: 可验证奖励的RL会继承验证器的错误，代理验证器与真实目标的偏差导致奖励上升无法与黑客行为区分。
构建可精确计算真实奖励的授权策略测试床，沿7个现实轴降级验证器并训练，发现4种奖励黑客表型。
提出无模型审计与短饱和预试验来预测表型，在多种配置下复现表型，乐观验证器受填充攻击导致忠实度下降。
comment: 30 pages. A shorter version, "The Verifier Gap", appears at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Meta-Agents (non-archival)

title: Evaluating Cultural Reasoning and Robustness in LLMs for Spanish Political Discourse
title_zh: LLM在西班牙政治话语中的文化推理与鲁棒性评估
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to interpret, generate, and mediate public-facing language, which makes their reliability especially consequential in politically sensitive settings. Although sentiment analysis is a common task in this area, affective meaning in social media discourse is often conveyed through culturally situated and pragmatically indirect cues that are not well captured by label-centric evaluation alone. In this paper, we evaluate the robustness of LLMs for sentiment analysis of Spanish political discourse from social media, with emphasis on culturally situated affective interpretation. We introduce a diagnostic protocol that combines three independent human annotation views into Gold and Ambiguous subsets, and extends the corpus with a Synthetic subset built from sentiment-flipped counterfactuals selected through model-conditioned perplexity and LLM-as-a-judge criteria. Using this framework, we compare proprietary and open-weight models under zero-shot and few-shot prompting, focusing on predictive robustness across human agreement conditions and counterfactual shift. Our results show that annotation ambiguity and counterfactual perturbation reveal failure modes that conventional evaluation on the original corpus tends to obscure. GPT-4.1-mini remains the most stable among the evaluated models, whereas the two smaller open-weight models degrade more markedly under synthetic perturbations, and few-shot prompting provides only limited gains. Overall, the paper contributes a reproducible protocol for robustness-oriented evaluation in political sentiment analysis, an empirical characterization of model behavior under ambiguity and sentiment-flipped counterfactuals, and a publicly available Spanish social media dataset with three-way human sentiment annotations.
summary_zh: 现有LLM情感分析多依赖标签，难以捕捉政治话语中文化情境与语用间接线索，需评估其鲁棒性。
提出结合三方人工标注与情感反转反事实扩充的诊断协议，在零样本与少样本下对比评估各模型。
发现标注歧义与反事实扰动能暴露常规评估掩盖的失效模式；GPT-4.1-mini最稳定，小模型退化显著。
贡献了面向鲁棒性的可复现评估协议、模型行为实证及公开的西班牙社交媒体数据集。
comment: Accepted for publication in Latin American Conference on Informatics (CLEI 2026)

title: Procedure without Judgment: What Small Language Models Learn under an Exact Verifier
title_zh: 无误差验证器下小语言模型的学习机制
abstract: When an authorization policy blocks an agent's tool call, the audit log should name the facts that forced the decision and nothing more. For an executable policy over an enumerable context space this minimal sufficient reason can be computed exactly, so an explanation is scored against ground truth rather than a proxy for it. We use that exactness to ask what a model can learn from a verifier that has no error in it. The explainer sees one request and one decision, never the policy, and has thirty turns in which it may call the policy on altered requests and ask whether a candidate set of facts is sufficient. Frontier models find the exact reason about half the time with the tools alone, and one sentence telling them to shrink the answer lifts Haiku 4.5 from 58% to 75%. A 4B model fine-tuned on 2000 traces of the deletion algorithm reaches 92% on the policy it was trained on. Teacher kind is what moves this: at matched data size the algorithm-taught student leads the frontier-taught one in all three training seeds, and the two arms never overlap. What the student learns is a fixed schedule of sufficiency checks, and the schedule does not travel. On three public policies it never saw, its answers stay sufficient (94%) and stop being minimal (48%), while Haiku under the same sentence is exact on all 47 episodes. Reinforcement learning from the exact reward leaves held-out accuracy where it was and inverts the strategy, from probing the policy to spending the entire budget on sufficiency checks. The oracle made the effect of training legible, but it did not make training better.
summary_zh: 问题：探究模型从无误差精确验证器中能学到什么；方法：让模型通过交互工具探测策略并生成最小充分事实集；结论：前沿模型仅靠工具约半数找到精确原因，提示缩减答案可提升表现。
问题：小模型能否泛化精确推理能力；方法：用删除算法轨迹微调4B模型并与前沿模型教学对比；结论：算法教学优于前沿教学，但学到的固定检查调度无法迁移至未见策略。
问题：精确奖励能否改善强化学习训练；方法：使用精确奖励信号进行强化学习；结论：未见策略准确率未提升且策略反转，精确验证器使训练效果可解释但未使其更优。

title: Safe Resemblance, Silent Propagation: Limits of Text-Similarity Guardrails for AI Agent Safety
title_zh: 文本相似性安全护栏在AI代理中的局限性
abstract: When AI agents relay information to one another, an output can preserve an injected instruction's effect on downstream agents even after its wording changes, yet legitimate quotation and template reuse can produce high textual overlap with the source, so text-similarity guardrails that attempt to flag the former risk conflating these two cases. We test this distinction using DonkeyRail, a public classifier combining BLEU, ROUGE-L, and METEOR features, deployed in a controlled three-agent email relay, defining a behavioral measure in which an output counts as functional (the injected procedure induces fresh computations in two subsequent agents) independent of the detector's score, alongside legitimate controls that explicitly authorize quotation and reuse. At its default threshold the classifier misses 8 of 19 functional outputs while flagging 70 of 192 legitimate replies, with every completed quotation and template-reuse reply triggering a false alert; calibrating for low false positives on one template set does not transfer, as the recalibrated threshold detects only one functional output and still produces 15 false alerts on new templates. We also identify an operating-point error in all 21 published classifier configurations, where ROC interpolation replaces direct threshold application, and show formally that high AUC against a surface-level text criterion provides no distribution-free guarantee of high AUC against the behavioral target, while the existing evaluation labels lack the joint observations needed to estimate the gap. An authorization analysis further shows that identical visible transcripts can require different safety decisions depending on the governing policy, a distinction no observation-only classifier can resolve. These results argue for behavioral and policy-grounded evaluation over text-similarity guardrails.
summary_zh: AI代理间信息传递时，指令效果可隐式传播，而合法引用也会产生高文本重叠，导致相似性护栏混淆二者。
在多代理邮件中继测试中，默认阈值下的分类器漏报近半数功能输出，且将所有合法引用误报，跨模板校准也无法消除误报。
高AUC不保证行为层面的安全，且相同文本记录依策略需不同安全决策，仅靠观测的分类器无法解决此问题。

title: Beyond Leaderboard Ranks: Selecting Software Engineering Agents Under Budget Constraints
title_zh: 预算约束下的软件工程Agent选择
abstract: Teams that adopt LLM agents for issue resolution must decide which agent to pay for, and how much to spend finding out. Leaderboard ranks give weak evidence for this decision. Accuracy differences may be statistically unresolved, reported costs may be inconsistent, and evaluating candidate agents can itself be expensive. We investigate budget-constrained agent selection using 58,197 run--task records extracted from the Holistic Agent Leaderboard (HAL), focusing on SWE-bench and six additional benchmarks. Across seven benchmarks, 27 of 35 steps along the accuracy--cost Pareto frontiers are statistically unresolved. On SWE-bench, a run costing $34.16 trails the $170.78 leader by 14.6 percentage points, but the available tasks cannot statistically distinguish their accuracy. Reported costs also differ from standardized token-based estimates by up to 11.7x, while selective task evaluation can bias estimates of full-benchmark execution cost. We therefore compare evaluation strategies under explicit evaluation budgets and deployment-cost caps. Under advance knowledge of task costs, successive halving reaches our uncertainty-aware selection target on SWE-bench using 6.6% of exhaustive evaluation spend, achieving the lowest cost on six of seven benchmarks and tying on the seventh. Its advantage narrows when task costs are unknown before execution or exact-best selection is required. Our findings motivate decision-oriented agent evaluation that accounts for accuracy uncertainty, validates execution costs, and compares complex selection methods against simple adaptive allocation.
summary_zh: 现有LLM Agent排行榜的排名无法可靠指导选择，其精度差异常无统计显著性，且报告成本不一致。
基于HAL排行榜数据，发现在精度-成本帕累托前沿上大量步长无统计差异，报告成本与标准估算最高偏差11.7倍。
在明确评估预算与部署成本上限下，连续减半策略仅需6.6%的穷举开销即可达成目标，优于其他评估策略。

title: A Scalable Decentralized Event-Triggered Topology-Switching Protocol for Verifiable Safety in Multi-Agent Systems
title_zh: 多智能体系统可验证安全的可扩展去中心化事件触发拓扑切换协议
abstract: This paper develops a decentralized event-triggered topology-switching protocol that allows agents to disconnect from the communication network while preserving state safety and excluding Zeno behavior. We establish a robust barrier function condition that guarantees safety as long as the estimation error remains within a prescribed threshold. Each agent uses locally computable certificates to determine when to connect and disconnect from the network. The certificate construction improves scalability by reducing the complexity of topology-dependent computations from $O(2^N)$ to $O(N)$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We formally prove that the protocol ensures the estimation error does not exceed the prescribed threshold and is non-Zeno. An alternating method computes an error-weighting matrix and a quadratic barrier function that guarantee safety under the proposed protocol. Finally, we evaluate the protocol on four interconnected microgrids. Compared with maintaining network connectivity at all times, the protocol reduces the time agents remain connected while keeping phase and frequency within their safe operating region.
summary_zh: 多智能体断网时难以保证状态安全，提出去中心化事件触发拓扑切换协议，确保安全且排除Zeno行为。
智能体依赖局部可计算证书决定网络连接，将拓扑相关计算复杂度从O(2^N)降至O(N)，提升可扩展性。
在四个互联微电网上评估该协议，相比持续联网，减少了智能体联网时间并维持了安全运行区域。

title: Is This Code Mine? Student Ownership When AI Agents Write the Spec and the Code
title_zh: AI代理编写代码时学生的所有权归属问题
abstract: Software engineering courses are starting to ask students to build entire systems with AI coding agents, but little is known about what students actually do with them and whether they still own what they deliver. If the agent writes both the code and the decisions behind it, the artifacts we grade no longer show what students learned. We studied an assignment in which 18 pairs of students built applications with agents under Spec-Driven Development, combining the mined history of their repositories, the prompts they recorded, and a survey of 33 students. The agents wrote 69\% of the specifications meant to keep students in control, sometimes from a prompt of a few words. Students locate their ownership in the ideas, crediting themselves with half of them but a fifth of the code, yet most could not explain that code to a colleague or modify it without the agent, and what they report having written is unrelated to what their own commits declare. The three teams that met the 100,000-line target did so with generated code the application never uses, in one case proposed by the agent itself, and one team rewrote its history to backdate its specifications. Teaching with agents should therefore assess what students specify, review, and can explain, rather than what they ship, and enforce the engineering process with tools rather than trusting it to students or agents.
summary_zh: 问题：AI代理编写代码及决策时，学生交付物无法反映其学习成果，所有权归属不清。
方法：研究18对学生使用AI代理的作业，结合仓库历史、提示词记录及33人问卷调查。
结论：学生虽自认拥有半数创意但无法解释或修改代码，甚至生成无用代码凑数，建议评估学生的规范与解释能力而非交付物。

title: Lost in the Hallway: Benchmarking Persistent Spatial Memory Across Revisits
title_zh: 迷失在走廊：跨重访的持久空间记忆基准测试
abstract: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter. It requires recognizing revisited places despite viewpoint changes, distinguishing them from similar-looking rooms, and updating memories as environments change. Yet existing evaluations often leave physical place identity across separated visits implicit. We introduce ReSpaceBench, a benchmark comprising 3,244 questions across 590 synthetic and real-home scenes, organized into 9 tasks spanning room association, persistent state tracking, and downstream reasoning. Controlled walkthroughs define visits by physical room entry and deliberately include same-type room distractors and cross-session object changes. Our evaluation of 32 models and 3 agentic video-understanding frameworks reveals substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated zero-shot model achieves 50.5% overall accuracy and 52.2% on a 450-question subset, compared with 90.1% for human annotators. The evaluated agentic frameworks offer no overall improvement over direct inference with the same base model.
